reviews.review: It's like Skyrim with guns... and in space... with alien bugs.

What a banging video game. The game feels limitless with exciting tasks and unique terrain. Each mission feels like a challenge and no matter what you do, you can't stop enjoying it. Need a game to relax to, or want to try your very hardest to survive? Just change up the difficulty level and enjoy playing the game, exactly how you want to. I'd probably consider this the best video game created since 2016. If by some sort of miracle the developers are reading this. Thank you soo much for creating this game! 

Lastly would I recommend this game? Hell f*cking yeah I would!

A great allegory about the working class. There's nothing like getting back from the job and having a nice beer and dance with your peers. 

The symbolism behind this game is amazing.

As a mining company, you will no doubt see the creators have made the usually soul sucking, red tape laden, and physically taxing work that mining is, into a very fun filled adventure game.

The glyphids represent the red tape that you have to get through to get anything done, like making sure the local species will be fine during operations, as well as making sure the local biome itself is relatively safe from harm.

The weapons and armor represent the fact that to be a decent miner/mining company, you have to have access to some great capital, or your mining endeavors will be short lived, as well as the importance of having a good physique. 

The class system represents how diverse of employment a mining company actually uses. I especially love how the scout is seemingly useless, like the geologist who had sex with my wife, only to still stick around because he has a skill set that comes in handy in 6% of the situations that are actually required to survive that instance. 

The home-base system represents the end of a long day's work, where you get dressed up in a mirror to spend about a few moments with your brothers of Rock and Stone drinking beer and having a dance. This especially hit home to me since I met my ex-wife at a strip club after a mining op we had in Canada, and the feeling of relief yet regret after a DRG run was very close to that feeling I had when I married Christine.

But in all seriousness, if you like co-op shooters with a large amount of objectives, this game is for you. 10/10, would play more if I wasn't sucked into other games atm.

Great community, play at your own pace so it's as sweaty or easy as you like and enough variety to keep the game fresh for a long time.

Very easy to play for a few weeks and then return to in a couple months time, as it's PvE there's no evolving meta or way of being left behind.
